newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine grain trade feels impact of 96 export curb.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine grain trade feels impact of 96 export curb.

text.p: Ukraine's agricultural trade is in difficult financial straits after the government last year secretly and temporarily banned grain exports, the president of a group of private agriculture businesses said on Thursday.

"Last year's harvest was the worst for many years. But its bad effects were multiplied by government actions preventing the movement of grain," said Leonid Kozachenko, president of the Ukrainian League of Entrepreneurs of the Agroindustrial Complex.
"This has created serious financial problems for all of us."
Ukraine has never formally admitted to having quietly ordered state-owned elevators to lock up grain last August until state grain purchase contracts were fulfilled.
But traders, brokers, commodities exchanges and private businesses who lost millions of dollars because they could not meet export contracts talk of the ban as fact.
"This prevented our companies from receiving payment from our customers for the inputs which we supplied last spring," Kozachenko said.
Ukrainian grain is often exported to former Soviet republics, including Russia, and to Eastern Europe.

The league represents about 1,500 private businesses in the agriculture sector. It began a two-day conference on Thursday in a bid to win support to reform a farm sector still heavily controlled by a Soviet-style government.

"Unfortunately, actions by the state continue to create difficulties for our businesses," Kozachenko said. "The economic and legal climate for the development of market relations is still unfavourable and shows no signs of improvement."

Ukraine, which has forecast a grain harvest of 35 million tonnes this year, has blamed drought for last year's poor 25.4 million tonne harvest -- but Western experts have also cited chronic shortages of fuel, machinery and money.
Kozachenko said that more than 80 percent of the sector was now financed privately.
